stem.text: A particle moves in the xy-plane so that its position at time t is \( \left(x(t), y(t)\right) = \left( - \frac{t^{3}}{3} + 3 t,\ - \frac{t^{2}}{4} + 3 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 6 \right) \) for \( 0 \le t \le 2 \). Using a calculator where needed, find all times t in the open interval \( 0 < t < 2 \) at which the particle is moving toward the x-axis. Give a reason for your answer, and give any decimal endpoint correct to three decimal places.

answer_key.label: The particle moves toward the x-axis for \( 0 < t < 1.345 \), because \( y(t) \) and \( y'(t) \) have opposite signs there.

worked_solution.text: Since \( \sin t \le 1 \), \( y(t) \le -3 \) for every t, so \( y(t) \) is negative and the particle stays on one side of the x-axis.

The particle moves toward the x-axis when \( y(t) \) and \( y'(t) \) have opposite signs, that is, when \( y'(t) = - \frac{t}{2} + 3 \cos{\left(t \right)} > 0 \). A calculator gives \( y'(t) = 0 \) at \( t \approx 1.345 \), with \( y'(t) \) positive before that time and the opposite sign after it.
So the particle moves toward the x-axis for \( 0 < t < 1.345 \), because there \( y(t) < 0 \) and \( y'(t) > 0 \), so its distance from the x-axis, \( |y(t)| \), is decreasing.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign analysis of the velocity component

options.label: The particle moves toward the x-axis for \( 0 < t < 1.345 \), because \( y(t) \) and \( y'(t) \) have opposite signs there.
The particle moves toward the x-axis for \( 1.345 < t < 2 \), because \( y'(t) \) is negative there.
options.derivation: approaching read as a negative rate, so the times with y'(t) < 0 taken without the sign of y(t)

options.derivation: the other velocity component used, so the times with x'(t) > 0 reported
